title: SWPC geomagnetic K-index warnings in 2013-2026 came before 94-95% of storm alerts, but mostly within the 44-minute L1 transit time; storm watch days reached the watched level in only 19-30%
abstract: We tested two NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) products: short-term geomagnetic K-index warnings (G1 to G3+) and one-to-three-day storm watches. We used all SWPC messages in the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive from 2002 to November 2026. Outcomes were SWPC's own K-index alerts and GFZ definitive Kp. We used only days with complete archive coverage. In 2013-2026 a warning was in effect before 95.3% of 639 K5 alert episodes, 95.0% of 202 K6 episodes and 93.5% of 62 K7+ episodes. The median lead was 66, 38 and 25 minutes. Only 50.7%, 38.1% and 30.6% had at least 60 minutes of lead (95% block intervals 46.6-54.5%, 31.0-45.2%, 20.5-40.9%). SWPC sudden impulse messages give a median shock transit from the L1 monitor to the ground of 44 minutes (n = 199). In storms that followed a shock, the warning was issued after the shock passed L1 in 57 of 69 K5, 42 of 45 K6 and 20 of 22 K7+ episodes, and before it in 7, 1 and 1. On the GFZ three-hour scale, a warning came before the first storm-level interval in only 35%, 24% and 15% of episodes. False-alarm ratios were 28%, 29% and 17%. A rule that warns level n when level n-1 is reached gave longer K6-K7 leads but 72-73% false alarms. Since the G-scale watch format (September 2012), the watched level was reached on 30.2% of 633 G1-watched days, 25.6% of 156 G2 days and 18.9% of 37 G3 days. On G3-watched days with no sudden impulse, G3 occurred on 1 of 16. Only 49.5% of G1+ days had a prior G1+ watch. Thus warnings give near-complete coverage but lead times limited by L1 monitoring, and the day-ahead information in watches is mostly not reached. Limitations: outcomes come mainly from SWPC's own real-time index; about 3-5% of messages are missing from the archive; episode definitions affect lead (sensitivity 43-65% at K5 for 1 h); driver classification by sudden impulses is exploratory. Code, the SWPC message snapshot, aggregate results and a reproduction script are included; GFZ records stay external.
